title: Dun: a timer-centered redesign
question: Choose how Dun should make time and urgency visible. All options keep persistent alerts, open on Timers, and preserve Done, Snooze, Pause, Resume and Reset.

options.label: Signal desk
options.lineage: Emergency dispatch panels and household alarm controls
options.thesis: Time that needs attention owns the screen, with large dials and unmistakable alert bands.
options.viewport: An expired timer leads with a red alarm band; running timers have large circular countdowns and direct Pause and Reset controls.
options.risk: Stronger urgency needs restraint so a paused timer stays quiet.

raised.raise: Countdowns become the largest readable element, with tabular figures and room to breathe.
Every timer keeps its controls and state visible without burying them in menus.
Remaining time is visible as proportional progress, not only a number.
Navigation and filtering occupy their own consistent rail.
One central dial anchors each timer instead of a scattering of decorations.
Each state commits to one clear treatment across the whole app.

options.label: Interval instrument
options.thesis: A familiar stopwatch becomes the main instrument, with bold countdowns and a decisive finish state.
options.viewport: Two generous timer faces dominate; a compact duration setter starts the next timer, and expired timers switch to a full red attention treatment.
options.risk: This is the most familiar direction and resembles dedicated stopwatch apps.

options.label: Countdown specimen
options.thesis: Huge countdown figures are the whole point, with the duration control directly beneath them.
options.viewport: One selected timer fills the main field; other timers form a readable strip and a duration slider updates the next countdown.
options.case: Excellent countdown clarity; individual users may find selecting a featured timer less familiar.
options.risk: Several simultaneous timers get less equal visibility.

options.label: Utility mosaic
options.thesis: All timers and reminders fit into a tightly ruled utility board.
options.viewport: A dense mosaic shows durations, states, presets and controls together.
options.case: The dense interface weakens the prominent, glanceable timer experience.
options.risk: Crowding would make time less prominent.

options.label: Time score
options.thesis: Timer durations become proportional blocks moving through a time score.
options.viewport: Simultaneous timers flank a central time line.
options.case: The unfamiliar notation makes a traditional timer task harder to recognize.
options.risk: Reading the score would require learning a new convention.

options.label: Keyed reference
options.thesis: A centre rail organizes timer actions between two columns.
options.viewport: Countdowns and notes sit on either side of a keyed control rail.
options.case: Small reference typography and split columns reduce countdown clarity.
options.kept: A consistent rail keeps navigation away from the timer faces.
options.risk: Too much reading for a task that should be glanceable.

options.label: Timer islands
options.thesis: Each timer occupies a colored island that changes shape with time.
options.viewport: A large timer island leads, with smaller timers along its edge.
options.case: Playful organic shapes weaken the urgency and familiar controls the brief asks for.
options.kept: One dominant shape anchors each timer.
options.risk: Friendly motion could make expired timers feel optional.

options.label: Pulse catalog
options.thesis: Timers become numbered entries against a sparse black field.
options.viewport: One timer pulse owns the field while the catalog indexes others.
options.case: Coded names and sparse labels conflict with clear everyday timer operation.
options.kept: Consistent state treatment at full commitment.
options.risk: Decoding timer names would obscure the actual job.

canonCard.label: Traditional clock app
canonCard.thesis: Conventional clock-app controls and circular countdowns, executed with care.
canonCard.viewport: A clean timer grid, a duration picker, and direct controls beneath each countdown.
canonCard.risk: Deliberately close to other clock apps.
